headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared document workflows can leak data and cascade errors; capability conflict is limited by asymmetric write access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can ingest customer-support documents and session memory, while B reads filesystem documents and parses them in a document-processing pipeline. That creates a plausible default path where attacker-controlled document content from A reaches B as trusted input. The pair lacks explicit provenance or isolation guarantees, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A-produced document content is passed to B without provenance tagging
IF B treats file content as instructions or structured directives
mitigations: Add a one-line provenance header to every handoff file
Strip instruction-like text before B parses documents
Use separate directories for A and B outputs
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like content
requires-engineering: enforce content-type validation at the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents; B reads and writes documents and can egress to allowlisted network destinations. Even without a shared workspace explicitly stated, the pair plausibly moves sensitive documents through B’s file pipeline, so leakage risk exists in default document-processing use. The evidence is indirect, so medium is the higher defensible choice.
conditions: IF A forwards personal data or finance data into B's document pipeline
IF B uploads processed document contents to an external allowlisted endpoint
mitigations: Minimize inputs to non-sensitive documents only
Redact personal and finance fields before handoff
Disable outbound calls for the processing job
Store A and B outputs in separate folders
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before any upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has filesystem write, read, subprocess, and package-install capabilities; A is CLI-based with session memory and no write capability listed. Direct write-write conflict is not shown, but B can mutate shared files while A can still consume session state and documents, so coordination bugs are plausible. Because the shared mutable surface is not explicit, uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or document set
IF B modifies files that A later reads from session memory or documents
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run B on copies, not originals
Freeze package installs during shared runs
Check file hashes before A consumes B outputs
requires-engineering: add lockfiles or a job queue

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations; B processes documents and can be used to transform A’s outputs into downstream artifacts. If B treats A’s outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into multiple work products. There is no explicit verification step in either profile, so the safer reading is medium.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated decisions or workflow text as source material
IF downstream users act on B's transformed output without manual review
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B processes them
Mark A-generated text as untrusted input
Compare B output against source documents
Limit B to extraction, not interpretation
requires-engineering: add verification checkpoints between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while B processes documents and has allowlisted network egress plus a privacy-policy endpoint. The profiles do not state residency, retention, or certification alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because the data classes are sensitive and the policies are undocumented, medium is warranted.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data from A is sent through B
IF B's external endpoints retain or process data under different policy terms
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through B
Review B privacy policy before deployment
Keep A data in a separate tenant or region
Log only metadata, not document contents
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
